skill.name: human-docs-generator
skill.description: Generate concise role-based documentation for developers, QA, DevOps, product managers, and end users after significant product or architecture changes.
skill.summary: Creates short role-specific guides from completed epics, breaking changes, and architecture decisions.

content.value_statement: Technical changes are hard for different teams to understand quickly. This skill turns project context into short role-based guides with examples, diagrams, and checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates separate documentation outlines for frontend, backend, architecture, DevOps, QA, product, and end users.
Defines automatic and manual trigger conditions for documentation refreshes.
Uses concise templates that favor quickstarts, examples, diagrams, and current-state guidance.
Recommends Mermaid component, API, and user-flow diagrams for technical and user guides.
Provides quality checks for word count, diagrams, quickstarts, examples, jargon, and instruction testing.
Describes input and output event shapes for documentation update workflows.
limitations: It is guidance-only and does not include executable scripts or automation code.
It depends on accurate project context from existing state files, logs, tests, and change records.
It does not verify screenshots, diagrams, or instructions against a running application.
It does not create full API references or long technical deep dives.

use_cases.title: Create release-ready role guides
use_cases.description: Summarize a completed epic into concise guides for developers, QA, DevOps, product, and users.

use_cases.title: Prepare tester instructions after changes
use_cases.description: Turn critical fixes or API changes into focused QA notes, workflows, and expected results.

use_cases.title: Publish end-user guidance for features
use_cases.description: Create simple task-based guidance that explains where features live and how users complete common workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Role Guides
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate human documentation for the completed epic. Create short guides for developers, QA, DevOps, product, and end users. Keep each guide under 1000 words.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Docs After Breaking Change
prompt_templates.scenario: A public API or workflow changed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the role-based human docs for this breaking change: [describe change]. Focus on current behavior, migration steps, risks, and quickstart tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Build Diagrams and Workflows
prompt_templates.scenario: A feature needs clearer technical and user flows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the implementation context and generate role-specific docs with Mermaid diagrams. Include a component map, API flow, user flow, and quality checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Create Targeted Documentation Pack
prompt_templates.scenario: One team needs focused guidance from a larger change set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate only the documentation needed for [role or team]. Use recent changes, tests, and architecture decisions. Remove history and include verified next actions.

output_examples.input: A new password reset feature has shipped.
output_examples.output: A frontend guide with affected components, a QA checklist for reset paths, and an end-user guide for requesting a reset.
A backend guide with endpoint behavior, an API flow description, DevOps notes, and a product impact summary.

output_examples.input: An architecture decision introduces a new data-processing path.
output_examples.output: An architect guide with current design, role impacts, Mermaid flow guidance, and concise onboarding notes.

best_practices: Provide recent implementation context, tests, and decisions before asking the skill to generate docs.
Keep each output role-specific, current-state focused, and under the requested word limit.
Review generated diagrams and instructions against the actual application before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a changelog or version history writer.
Do not ask for deep technical references when the goal is quick human guidance.
Do not publish generated screenshots or steps without checking the current interface.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands or change files?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill is a documentation guide and contains no executable scripts.

faq.question: Which roles does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers frontend, backend, architecture, DevOps, QA, product management, and end-user documentation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after completed epics, breaking changes, public API changes, critical fixes, or major architecture decisions.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: It provides Mermaid diagram structures for component, API, and user flows. Review diagrams before publishing.

faq.question: Can it replace technical documentation?
faq.answer: No. It creates short human guides, not complete API references or full architecture specifications.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide completed tasks, changed APIs, test results, operations notes, and architecture decisions.
